item.title: Management
item.description:
Well-Known

The /.well-known/ prefix provides locations for management resources, following the conventions in RFC 8615.

Get health status

GET /.well-known/health
Returns the health status of the current heimdall instance for monitoring and health checks.

Responses

  • 200: The current health status.

    application/json

    Example

    {
 "status": "ok"
}
    Schema
    Health status object
    Basic health information for the current heimdall instance.
    status string
    The health status

  • 500: Internal Server Error. Returned when the service cannot process the request because of an internal error.

Get JWT verification keys

GET /.well-known/jwks

Returns the public keys needed to verify JWTs issued by heimdall as a JSON Web Key Set (RFC 7517). The contents reflect the configured key store.

Responses use an ETag for caching. A client can send the previously received value using If-None-Match; unchanged content results in HTTP 304 Not Modified.

Parameters

  • If-None-Match: string (header, optional)

    The ETag received from an earlier JWKS response. If it still matches, heimdall responds with HTTP 304 Not Modified.
    Carries the ETag value from the previous response. Enables the client to check whether there is a change to the server side resource. Example: If-None-Match: "33a64df551425fcc55e4d42a148795d9f25f89d4".

Responses

  • 200: JWKS containing verification keys and optional certificate chains.

    Response headers

    • ETag

      string
      The ETag (or entity tag) HTTP response header is an identifier for a specific version of a resource. It lets caches be more efficient and save bandwidth, as a web server does not need to resend a full response if the content was not changed. Example: ETag: "33a64df551425fcc55e4d42a148795d9f25f89d4".

    application/json

    Example

    {
 "keys": [
 {
 "alg": "ES384",
 "crv": "P-384",
 "kid": "foo",
 "kty": "EC",
 "use": "sig",
 "x": "0WuRhXd8TpGy8Xn3zDT3xkkS7Ua66QQSK69gWxPHw7k1tZyQXsUuEudYDb_vwN9f",
 "x5c": [
 "",
 "",
 ""
 ],
 "y": "_CBaqh43zjEowNq1wZcrMr-bdeDHdz17iVSkJKYonUzDFeyuiHETAQrYcqDT_8mG"
 },
 {
 "alg": "ES384",
 "crv": "P-384",
 "kid": "bar",
 "kty": "EC",
 "use": "sig",
 "x": "F47uZNn_QtqKXcxsYsJSc5asaqEPxVuc2sIVLzR2dRDi29tdA_X7phRX9kGhDnOO",
 "y": "elcChdCImsIaRT7xVLslehBpVaWKlNnCSTPhJLYXwcB1dS24bpUkwAiVijejZ0J0"
 }
 ]
}
    Schema
    JSON Web Key Set object
    Public keys used to verify JWTs issued by heimdall, in JSON Web Key Set format.
    keys array required
    The value of the ‘keys’ parameter is an array of JWK values. By default, the order of the JWK values within the array does not imply an order of preference among them, although applications of JWK Sets can choose to assign a meaning to the order for their purposes, if desired.
    Array items
    object
    alg string
    Identifies the algorithm intended for use with the key
    crv string
    The name of the curve, if the entry represents an EC key (see RFC 7518 for more details)
    e string
    Exponent parameter of an RSA public key, if the entry represents an RSA public key
    key_ops string
    Identifies the operation(s) for which the key is intended to be used
    kid string
    The identifier of the key
    kty string required
    Identifies the cryptographic algorithm family used with the key, such as ‘RSA’ or ‘EC’
    n string
    Modulus parameter of an RSA public key, if the entry represents an RSA public key (see RFC 7518 for more details)
    use string
    Identifies the intended use of the public key, such as ‘sig’, or ’enc’
    x string
    X parameter of the elliptic curve, if the entry represents an EC key
    x5c array
    Stands for an X.509 certificate chain. This parameter contains a chain of one or more PKIX certificates RFC5280. The certificate chain is represented as a JSON array of certificate value strings. Each string in the array is base64-encoded
    Array items
    string
    x5t string
    Stands for X.509 certificate SHA-1 thumbprint. This parameter is a base64url-encoded SHA-1 thumbprint (a.k.a. digest) of the DER encoding of an X.509 certificate RFC5280
    x5t#S256 string
    Stands for X.509 certificate SHA-256 thumbprint. This parameter is a base64url-encoded SHA-256 thumbprint (a.k.a. digest) of the DER encoding of an X.509 certificate RFC5280
    x5u string uri
    X.509 URL parameter is a URI RFC3986 that refers to a resource for an X.509 public key certificate or certificate chain RFC5280.
    y string
    Y parameter of the elliptic curve, if the entry represents an EC key

  • 304: Not Modified. Returned when the resource has not changed since the supplied If-None-Match value.

  • 500: Internal Server Error. Returned when the service cannot process the request because of an internal error.

item.title: Main
item.description:
Main Service

This reference entry describes the request data used for access-control evaluation and the possible responses. See Rules for details of request matching.

Process an HTTP request

GET /{path_and_query_params}

This operation represents heimdall’s main HTTP request interface. It is not limited to GET. All other HTTP verbs are also supported and are subject to the configured rules. Method-specific HTTP semantics still apply: HEAD responses have no body, and configured CORS preflight OPTIONS requests can be handled without rule evaluation.

Requests may have nested paths and query strings. The path placeholder shown above is illustrative: it does not express a single-segment restriction on the requests that heimdall can process.

Response statuses and bodies depend on the matching rule and operating mode. In proxy mode, the upstream service determines the response, so its status codes are not limited to the examples listed below.

X-Forwarded-* and Forwarded headers are trusted only when the sender matches the configured trusted_proxies. Additional application-specific headers and cookies can be evaluated by the configured rules.

Parameters

  • path_and_query_params: string (path, required)

    Actual requested path, including any nested segments and optional query string, to be evaluated against the configured rules.

  • X-Forwarded-Method: string (header, optional)

    HTTP method to use for rule evaluation. Defaults to the method of the request received by heimdall when this header is absent.

  • X-Forwarded-Proto: string (header, optional)

    HTTP scheme to use when evaluating the request URL. When absent, heimdall uses the scheme of the incoming request.

  • X-Forwarded-Host: string (header, optional)

    Original request host to use when evaluating the request URL.

  • X-Forwarded-Uri: string (header, optional)

    Original request path and query string to use for rule evaluation.

  • X-Forwarded-For: string (header, optional)

    Client IP address information supplied by a trusted proxy.

  • Forwarded: string (header, optional)

    Standardized information about the original request and its proxy forwarding chain.

  • <Application Specific>: string (header, optional)

    Placeholder for other headers, the defined rules make use of.

  • <Application Specific>: string (cookie, optional)

    Placeholder for cookies, the defined rules make use of.

Responses

  • 200: A successful decision normally returns HTTP 200 in decision mode, unless a different status is configured. In proxy mode, an authorized request is forwarded and the upstream service determines the response status and body; HTTP 200 is only one possible result.

  • 400: Bad Request. Returned if the evaluated request path contains dot segments (. or ..), including URL-encoded variants (case-insensitive), e.g. %2e, %2f, and %5c combinations, to prevent path traversal.

  • 401: Unauthorized. Returned if a matching rule could not verify the authentication status of the subject related to the request.

  • 403: Forbidden. Returned if a matching rule could not verify the authorization status of the subject related to the request.

  • 404: Not Found. Returned if there was no rule found, which could be used to verify the request.

  • 405: Method Not Allowed. Returned if the matched rule does not permit the HTTP method.

  • 500: Internal Server Error. Returned when the service cannot process the request because of an internal error.

  • 502: Bad Gateway. Returned if communication with an upstream service fails, for example because of DNS or timeout errors.

item.title: Profiling
item.description:
Get available profiles

GET /debug/pprof
Lists the runtime profiles available on this heimdall instance. Use the profile-specific endpoint to retrieve a selected profile.

Responses

  • 200: List of available profiles

    text/html

    Schema
    string

Get a runtime profile

GET /debug/pprof/{profile_name}
Retrieves the selected runtime profile. Depending on the profile, query parameters control sampling duration, garbage collection, and the output format. Not every option applies to every profile.

Parameters

  • profile_name: string (path, required)

    Defines the profiling information to retrieve. Following profiles are available:

    • allocs - A sampling of all past memory allocations.
    • block - Stack traces that led to blocking on synchronization primitives.
    • cmdline - The command line invocation of the current program, with arguments separated by NUL bytes.
    • goroutine - Stack traces of all current goroutines.
    • heap - A sampling of memory allocations of live objects.
    • mutex - Stack traces of holders of contended mutexes.
    • profile - CPU profile. Profiling lasts for duration specified in seconds parameter, or for 30 seconds if not specified
    • symbol - Looks up the program counters listed in the request, responding with a table mapping program counters to function names.
    • threadcreate - Stack traces that led to the creation of new OS threads.
    • trace - Execution trace in binary form. Tracing lasts for duration specified in seconds parameter, or for 1 second if not specified.

  • seconds: integer (query, optional)

    Specifies the duration of sampling. Ignored, if the profile does not support sampling.

    If profile profile is used and this parameter is not specified, defaults to 30s.

    If trace profile is used and this parameter is not specified, defaults to 1s.

  • gc: integer (query, optional)

    Specifies for the heap profile whether the GC should be invoked before the sampling should be done. Any value > 0 means GC should be invoked.

  • debug: integer (query, optional)

    Specifies whether the profile information should be rendered as text and not in the profile.proto format. Any value > 0 means profile information should be rendered as text.

Responses

  • 200: The requested profiling information. If the debug query parameter was set to a value > 0 the MIME type of the response is text/html, otherwise it is application/octet-stream

    Response headers

    • Content-Disposition

      Set to attachment; filename="<used profile name>"
      string

    • X-Content-Type-Options

      Set to nosniff value.
      string

    application/octet-stream

    Schema
    string

    text/html

    Schema
    string

  • 400: Bad Request. Returned if the seconds parameter would exceed the server’s write timeout.

  • 404: Not Found. Returned if requested profile is not supported/known.

item.title: Metrics
item.description:
Get Prometheus metrics

GET /metrics
Returns metrics for scraping by Prometheus or compatible monitoring systems. The /metrics path is configurable and may differ between deployments.

Responses

  • 200: The metrics exposed by this heimdall instance.

    text/html

    Schema
    string

item.title: Validating Admission Controller
item.description:
Validate RuleSet

POST /validate-ruleset
Validates a heimdall RuleSet submitted in a Kubernetes AdmissionReview request and returns the admission decision with validation feedback.

Parameters

  • timeout: string (query, optional)

    Maximum duration allowed for validation, such as 5s or 250ms. Accepted units are ns, us, ms, s, m, and h.

    Example: 5s

Request body required

A Kubernetes AdmissionReview request containing the RuleSet to validate.

application/json
